q.t: Which of these statements is correct?
q.e: Gustav Holst's work includes The Planets, a suite of pieces themed around the planets of the solar system. Sir Edward Elgar's best-known work is probably the Pomp and Circumstance Marches; March No 1 is known as Land of Hope and Glory.
o: Sir Edward Elgar wrote The Planets

q.t: Which hymn did Gustav Holst adapt from part of The Planets suite?
q.e: He adapted Jupiter, part of the Planets suite, as the tune for I vow to thee my country, a popular hymn in British churches.
o: I vow to thee my country

q.t: Where was Henry Purcell the organist?
q.e: Henry Purcell (1659-95) was the organist at Westminster Abbey. He wrote church music, operas and other pieces, and developed a British style distinct from that elsewhere in Europe.

q.t: George Frederick Handel wrote the Water Music for which king?
q.e: The German-born composer George Frederick Handel spent many years in the UK and became a British citizen in 1727. He wrote the Water Music for King George I and Music for the Royal Fireworks for his son, George II.

q.t: Which TWO operas are among Benjamin Britten's best-known works?
q.e: Benjamin Britten (1913-76) is best known for his operas, which include Peter Grimes and Billy Budd. He also wrote A Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra, which is based on a piece of music by Purcell.

q.t: Which festival did Benjamin Britten found?
q.e: He founded the Aldeburgh festival in Suffolk, which continues to be a popular music event of international importance.

q.t: How long is the Proms season, and who has organised it?
q.e: The Proms is an eight-week summer season of orchestral classical music that takes place in various venues, including the Royal Albert Hall in London. It has been organised by the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) since 1927.
o: Eight weeks, organised by the BBC since 1927
Four weeks, organised by the BBC since 1927
Eight weeks, organised by the BBC since 1922
Two weeks, organised by the Royal Albert Hall

q.t: What is awarded each September for the best album from the UK and Ireland?
q.e: The Mercury Music Prize is awarded each September for the best album from the UK and Ireland. The Brit Awards is an annual event that gives awards in a range of categories, such as best British group and best British solo artist.

q.t: Which play has been running in the West End since 1952?
q.e: London's West End, also known as 'Theatreland', is particularly well known. The Mousetrap, a murder-mystery play by Dame Agatha Christie, has been running in the West End since 1952 and has had the longest initial run of any show in history.

q.t: Which TWO comic operas were written by Gilbert and Sullivan?
q.e: In the 19th century, Gilbert and Sullivan wrote comic operas, often making fun of popular culture and politics. These operas include HMS Pinafore, The Pirates of Penzance and The Mikado.

q.t: In a traditional British pantomime, who is the Dame?
q.e: One British tradition is the pantomime. Many theatres produce a pantomime at Christmas time. One of the traditional characters is the Dame, a woman played by a man. There is often also a pantomime horse or cow played by two actors.
o: A woman played by a man
A man played by a woman
A horse played by two actors

q.t: Which part of the Edinburgh Festival is the biggest and best known?
q.e: The Edinburgh Festival takes place in Edinburgh, Scotland, every summer. It is a series of different arts and cultural festivals, with the biggest and most well-known being the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, 'the Fringe'.
o: The Last Night of the Proms

q.t: After which British actor are the Laurence Olivier Awards named?
q.e: The Laurence Olivier Awards take place annually at different venues in London. The awards are named after the British actor Sir Laurence Olivier, later Lord Olivier, who was best known for his roles in various Shakespeare plays.
o: An actor best known for his roles in Shakespeare plays
A designer of Art Deco ceramics

q.t: In which year was the Turner Prize established, and where are the shortlisted works shown?
q.e: The Turner Prize was established in 1984 and celebrates contemporary art. It was named after Joseph Turner. Four works are shortlisted every year and shown at Tate Britain before the winner is announced.
o: 1984, and the works are shown at Tate Britain
1968, and the works are shown at Tate Britain
1984, and the works are shown at the National Gallery
1927, and the works are shown at Tate Modern

q.t: Which of these statements is correct?
q.e: John Constable (1776-1837) was a landscape painter most famous for his works of Dedham Vale on the Suffolk-Essex border in the east of England. Joseph Turner was an influential landscape painter in a modern style.
o: John Constable is most famous for his works of Dedham Vale
Joseph Turner is most famous for his works of Dedham Vale

q.t: Which TWO artists were members of the Pre-Raphaelites?
q.e: The Pre-Raphaelites were an important group of artists in the second half of the 19th century. They painted detailed pictures on religious or literary themes in bright colours. The group included Holman Hunt, Dante Gabriel Rossetti and Sir John Millais.

q.t: For what is Henry Moore best known?
q.e: Henry Moore (1898-1986) was an English sculptor and artist. He is best known for his large bronze abstract sculptures.

q.t: Which artist was a Welsh engraver and stained glass maker?
q.e: John Petts (1914-91) was a Welsh artist, best known for his engravings and stained glass. Sir John Lavery was a Northern Irish portrait painter.

q.t: Which building in the Tower of London is an example of a Norman castle keep?
q.e: The White Tower in the Tower of London is an example of a Norman castle keep, built on the orders of William the Conqueror.

q.t: Which TWO buildings did Inigo Jones design, taking inspiration from classical architecture?
q.e: In the 17th century, Inigo Jones took inspiration from classical architecture to design the Queen's House at Greenwich and the Banqueting House in Whitehall in London.

q.t: Who designed New Delhi to be the seat of government in India, and also the Cenotaph?
q.e: In the 20th century, Sir Edwin Lutyens had an influence throughout the British Empire. He designed New Delhi to be the seat of government in India. After the First World War, he was responsible for many war memorials, including the Cenotaph in Whitehall.

q.t: Which garden designer often said that a place had 'capabilities'?
q.e: In the 18th century, Lancelot 'Capability' Brown designed the grounds around country houses so that the landscape appeared to be natural, with grass, trees and lakes. He often said that a place had 'capabilities'.

q.t: Which annual show showcases garden design from Britain and around the world?
q.e: Gardens continue to be an important part of homes in the UK. The annual Chelsea Flower Show showcases garden design from Britain and around the world.

q.t: Which of these designers is associated with Art Deco ceramics?
q.e: Britain has produced many great designers, from Thomas Chippendale, who designed furniture in the 18th century, to Clarice Cliff, who designed Art Deco ceramics, to Sir Terence Conran, a 20th-century interior designer.
